title: Leaving VMware just got harder after Broadcom pulled VDDK downloads
summary: After Broadcom's acquisition of VMware, the company has pulled VDDK (Virtual Disk Development Kit) downloads, making it significantly harder for customers to migrate away from VMware to competing platforms. VDDK is essential for tools that perform VMware-to-cloud or VMware-to-hypervisor migrations, and its removal effectively creates a vendor lock-in barrier for enterprise customers.
problem_solved: Addresses the anti-competitive practice of restricting access to migration tools, preventing customers from exercising freedom to switch vendors.
why_valuable: Highlights the growing concern of vendor lock-in in enterprise software, where acquisitions can suddenly remove critical tools that businesses depend on for their infrastructure operations.
